blocks.text: I can explain how increasing or decreasing the minuend affects the difference.
In this lesson you will meet Alex and Jun. They will help you describe changes accurately using maths words.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The minuend is the number being subtracted from.
A subtrahend is a number subtracted from another.
The difference is the result after subtracting one number from another.
A constant is a quantity that has a fixed value that does not change or vary, such as a number.

blocks.text: Look at these equations. Picture each one on a ten frame with counters.

blocks.label: What’s the same? What’s different?
blocks.text: The subtrahend is the same in each one: it is 3. The minuend and the difference both increase by 10 each time.
If you {increase} the minuend and the subtrahend stays the same, the difference must increase by the same amount.
Jun makes a table. Read down the rows.
This time the minuend and difference decrease equally. The subtrahend is still constant. Constant means it stays the same.
If you {decrease} the minuend and the subtrahend remains constant, the difference must decrease by the same amount.

blocks.q: If I adjust the minuend and the subtrahend stays the same, I have to adjust the difference by the same amount. Which is the best reason?
options: Because the minuend and the subtrahend are never equal, so the difference needs changing.
Because the subtrahend is constant, the difference has to be adjusted to keep the equation balanced.
blocks.why: The subtrahend does not change, so the difference has to change by the same amount as the minuend to keep the equation balanced.

blocks.text: Alex has 36 p and Jun has 52 p before Jun finds 21 p down the back of his sofa. How many more pence does Jun have than Alex now?
Start with a bar model. Jun’s 52 p is the minuend and Alex’s 36 p is the subtrahend. The difference is 52 p − 36 p = **16 p**.

rows.note: Jun now has 73 p. The minuend went up by 21 p, so the difference goes up by 21 p.

blocks.label: Describe the change
blocks.text: I added 21 p to the minuend and kept the subtrahend the same. So I had to add 21 p to the difference.
Jun then buys a cupcake for 20 p. How many more pence does Jun have now?

rows.note: Jun’s 73 p becomes 53 p. Alex still has 36 p. 53 p is 36 p and 17 p.

blocks.label: Describe the change
blocks.text: I subtracted 20 p from the minuend and kept the subtrahend the same. So I had to subtract 20 p from the difference.

blocks.q: The subtrahend stays the same. Work out the new difference.

items.q: 80 p − 55 p = 25 p. The minuend goes up by 12 p. What is the new difference?
Zoe has 90 p and Ali has 42 p. Zoe spends 30 p. How many more pence does Zoe have than Ali now?
2.45 − 1.20 = 1.25. The minuend increases by 3. What is the new difference?

blocks.text: Alex makes a table. The subtrahend stays at 43,287 each time.
Going down the table, the minuend, and so the difference too, increase by 1,000. Going up the table, they decrease by 1,000 each time.
If you adjust the minuend and the subtrahend stays the same, the difference must adjust by the same amount.
Jun makes a table with decimal fractions. The subtrahend stays at 43.28.

blocks.label: What is the change in each row?
blocks.text: The minuend goes up by 10 each time. The subtrahend is constant, so the difference also goes up by 10. Going up the table, both decrease by 10.
Jun scores 63,500 points and Alex scores 43,200 points. Jun gets a bonus of 15,000 points for using a special move. How much did Jun win by?
Bar model: Jun’s score is the minuend, Alex’s score is the subtrahend. The difference is 63,500 − 43,200 = **20,300**.

rows.note: The bonus goes onto the minuend (Jun’s score becomes 78,500). Alex’s score stays the same, so the bonus goes onto the difference too.

blocks.label: Answer
blocks.text: Jun won by **35,300** points.
At the gift shop on a residential week, Alex has £12.50 and Jun has £7.35 left to spend. Alex spends £2.03 on penny sweets and chocolate. How much more does Alex have now?
The difference to begin with is £12.50 − £7.35 = **£5.15**. Alex’s £2.03 is taken away from the minuend, so it is taken away from the difference too.

rows.note: Alex has £10.47 now and Jun still has £7.35.

blocks.q: Use what happens to the difference when the minuend changes.

items.q: Kai scores 4,250 points and Lia scores 3,100. Kai gets a bonus of 500 points. How many more points does Kai have than Lia now?
1.22 − 0.54 = 0.68. The minuend decreases by 0.5. What is the new difference?

blocks.q: In each case the subtrahend stays the same. What happens to the difference?

items.text: A £5 voucher is added to the minuend
A penalty of 2,500 points is taken away from the minuend

items: If the minuend is adjusted and the subtrahend stays constant, the difference has to be adjusted by the same amount to keep an equation balanced.
This can be useful to find missing numbers and solve worded problems that feature adjustments to the minuend.

blocks.text: Minuend up and subtrahend the same = difference {up} by the same amount. Minuend down = difference {down} by the same amount.

flashcards.front: If I increase the minuend and keep the subtrahend the same, what happens to the difference?
flashcards.back:
It increases by the same amount.

6 − 3 = 3, 16 − 3 = 13

flashcards.front: If I decrease the minuend and keep the subtrahend the same, what happens to the difference?
flashcards.back:
It decreases by the same amount.

106 − 3 = 103, 96 − 3 = 93

flashcards.front: Why does the difference change by the same amount as the minuend?
flashcards.back: Because the subtrahend is constant, the difference has to be adjusted to keep the equation balanced.
A quantity that has a fixed value that does not change or vary.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Explain how increasing or decreasing the minuend affects the difference
worksheet.instructions: In every question the subtrahend stays the same. If the minuend changes, the difference changes by the same amount. Write each answer as a number.

questions.prompt: Sam has 64 p and Tia has 40 p. Sam finds 15 p. How many more pence does Sam have than Tia now?
questions.explanation: 64 p − 40 p = 24 p. Sam’s minuend went up by 15 p, so the difference goes up by 15 p: 24 + 15 = 39.

questions.prompt: 90 p − 42 p = 48 p. The minuend decreases by 30 p and the subtrahend stays the same. What is the new difference, in pence?
questions.explanation: The minuend decreases by 30, so the difference decreases by 30: 48 − 30 = 18.

questions.prompt: Jun scores 24,710 points and Alex scores 18,206 points. Jun gets a penalty of 2,500 points. How many points does Jun win by?
questions.explanation: 24,710 − 18,206 = 6,504. The penalty is taken off the minuend, so it is taken off the difference: 6,504 − 2,500 = 4,004.

questions.prompt: Alex has £10.47 and Jun has £7.35 left to spend. Alex wins a £5 shop voucher. How much more does Alex have than Jun now, in pounds?
questions.explanation: £10.47 − £7.35 = £3.12. The £5 is added to the minuend, so it is added to the difference: 3.12 + 5 = 8.12.
The minuend went up by 17,000 (59,922 to 76,922), so the difference goes up by 17,000: 16,635 + 17,000 = 33,635.
The minuend went up by 2,000, so the difference goes up by 2,000: 18,589 + 2,000 = 20,589.
The minuend went up by 21.5 (84.47 to 105.97), so the difference goes up by 21.5: 78.21 + 21.5 = 99.71.
